newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus president out of hospital after tests.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus president out of hospital after tests.

text.p: Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides was briefly admitted to hospital on Tuesday for heart tests prompted by a minor chest complaint but said he was feeling well after being discharged.

"I can assure you I am feeling very well," a relaxed -looking Clerides, 78, told reporters who surrounded him as he stepped out of an elevator on the ground floor of the Nicosia general hospital, heading back to the presidential palace.
Clerides underwent cardiac examinations earlier on Tuesday after feeling minor pains in his chest for two days. The visit was planned from Monday night by his doctors.
"I can't call it an illness, it was just a concern. The angeogram revealed circulation is very good along with everything else," Clerides said.
Doctors said the tests were satisfactory. "From our findings there is no cause for concern," cardiologist Costakis Zambartas said. He said the cause of the chest pains still had to be determined.

Government spokesman Manolis Christofides told journalists Clerides would keep up his official appointments and return to work on Wednesday. However an official visit to China scheduled for next week has been postponed, Christofides said.
Later this week Clerides is due to meet United Nations Under Secretary-General Sir Kieran Prendergast.
